newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index unchanged at 88 in April.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index unchanged at 88 in April.

text.p: The Conference Board's U.S. help-wanted advertising index was unchanged at 88.0 in April versus March, the Conference Board said on Thursday.

In the last three months, help-wanted advertising volume rose in six regions and fell in three. The largest increase -- 6.3 percent -- was registered in the Mountain region. It was followed by the West South Central increase of 4.0 percent, the Middle Atlantic at 3.1 percent, and the West and East North Central regions, both rising 2.0 percent.
"The labor market seems likely to tighten even more in the months ahead," Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein said.

"Given an already low 4.9 percent unemployment rate, that is good news for job seekers. Employers, however, are forced to offer higher wages to attract quality job candidates, at a time when it is difficult to raise prices," Goldstein added.
The Conference Board surveys advertising volume in 51 major newspapers across the country each month.
